transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm here because my wife suggested I come in. She's been a little worried, which I feel terrible about, honestly. I don't want to be a burden to her. But, um, I suppose for the past few weeks, my eating has just been a little... off? 

It's really nothing major, I promise. I just, I keep accidentally skipping breakfast and lunch. I just get busy or distracted and forget, you know? And then at dinner, even when she cooks something really nice—and she's a wonderful cook—I just kind of pick at it. I don't mean to be ungrateful at all. I just haven't had much of an appetite. I did notice my jeans are starting to feel a little loose, so I guess I've lost a bit of weight. Is that the kind of thing you need to know? I hope I'm explaining this right.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I'm completely miserable or anything like that. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining. But, um, I guess most days lately I do wake up with this kind of heavy, flat feeling? It's hard to explain. It's just like the apartment feels too quiet, you know? 

Usually, if I feel a little off, I'll pick up my guitar and play for a bit, and that helps. But lately, even doing that doesn't really lift my mood the way it normally would. I still try to play, of course, because I know I should keep up with my hobbies. But the interest just isn't fully there right now. Is it normal to feel like that sometimes? I really hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Um, my sleep? It's... it's mostly fine, really. I mean, I am getting some sleep, so I shouldn't complain. But, um, I guess it has been a little broken up lately? 

I don't know why, but I keep waking up around four or five in the morning. And once I'm up, my brain just sort of turns on. I start thinking about things I probably shouldn't be worrying about right then, like, um, the bills, or some of the music tracks I haven't finished. And then, because I've been up thinking, I end up feeling kind of tired before the day even really begins. 

I'm sure lots of people deal with that, right? Stress just keeping them up a bit? I try not to let it bother my wife, so I usually just stay quiet until her alarm goes off. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for?
How long have you been feeling this way overall?

Um, how long? Well, I suppose if I really think about it... it's been kind of lingering off and on for maybe three months? 

I mean, it wasn't terrible the whole time, I promise. It was just this sort of slowed-down, heavy feeling coming and going. I tried to just push through it and not make a fuss, you know? But I guess the past few weeks have been when it's felt the most... noticeable? Like with the sleep and the eating and everything. 

I really hope I haven't let this go on too long before coming in. I didn't want to waste anyone's time if it was just a passing phase. Does three months sound like a normal amount of time for something like this?
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, have you been more restless or fidgety lately?

Um, well... I definitely wouldn't say I'm restless or bouncing off the walls or anything. I try to stay pretty calm. But, um, I guess if I'm being completely honest, things do feel a bit... slower? 

It's not that I can't move, obviously. It's just... like, I'll sit there with my laptop open for ages, you know? Just staring at the screen for a long time before I even move my hands to type or, um, plug in the keyboard. It's like my body is just taking an extra second to catch up to what I want to do. 

I'm probably just being a little lazy, to be honest. I really try not to let it get in the way too much. Is it okay that I'm feeling a bit sluggish like that? I hope it's not too unusual.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you didn't need much sleep or felt like you could take on a lot more than usual?

Um, well... I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm an angry person or anything, because I really try to be easygoing. But, um, before this whole slowed-down phase started, I guess there was a bit of a stretch where I felt... I don't know, unusually fired up? 

It wasn't a bad thing at first! I actually felt like I was really on a roll, like I could get so much done. But, um, looking back, I might have been a little... easily annoyed? Like, if my wife asked me a simple question while I was working on something, I'd snap at her. Just because I felt like any small interruption was ruining my momentum, you know? 

I always felt terrible about it right after. I really don't like being irritable like that. I hope that doesn't make me sound awful? I think I just got a little too wrapped up in what I was doing, maybe. Is that the kind of thing you meant?
How long did that unusually energetic or irritable period last? Was it just a few days, or did it go on for weeks?

Um, let me think... I really want to give you the right answer here. I guess it wasn't a super long time? 

I don't think it was weeks and weeks, definitely not. Maybe just... a handful of days? Like, four or five days where I was just feeling a bit more keyed up and snappy than I should have been. I really tried to reel it in once I noticed I was being short with my wife, I promise. 

I hope that's not too bad? I mean, everyone has a few days where they're a little stressed and overdo it, right? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it okay. Does a few days sound like what you were looking for?
Have you ever had a period where you felt so good, or so irritable, that others noticed you were not your usual self, or where you got involved in activities that were unusual for you?

Um, well... I guess maybe people might have noticed I was a little more intense about my projects than usual? I don't think it was anything too crazy, though. I just get really focused sometimes.

Like, during those few days, I was just feeling really inspired, you know? I started making all these lists of musicians I wanted to contact. And, um, I was sending out a bunch of messages, trying to build these pitch decks, and planning out all these collaborations. All in the same week. 

I know it sounds like a lot, and I guess it was a bit more than I'd normally take on at once. But I was just trying to be productive! I really wasn't trying to cause any trouble or act weird. It's good to be driven sometimes, right? I hope it doesn't sound like I was totally out of control or anything. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where most of the time you felt down, lost interest in things, or experienced other symptoms like changes in appetite, sleep, or energy?

Um, well... I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself, because I do try to stay positive. But, um, yeah, I guess I have been feeling pretty down lately. 

I've been trying to shake it off, really I have. But looking back, I think this sort of... slowed-down, heavy feeling has been hanging around off and on for maybe about three months? It's just been a bit harder to get going, you know? And, um, the past few weeks have probably been the most noticeable. I just haven't had the energy to do much, even things I usually like. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or anything. I want to get back to my normal self, I really do. Does that sound like what you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Have you ever had a period lasting at least four days where you felt unusually good, extremely confident, or were doing things that were out of character for you, like spending a lot of money, taking on big projects, or acting impulsively?

Um, well... I guess during those few days I mentioned, when I was sending out all those messages and everything... I did feel really, really good about what I was doing. Like, maybe a bit more confident than usual? 

I really don't want to sound arrogant, I promise I'm usually pretty grounded. But I just... I honestly felt like I had finally cracked the whole music-tech thing, you know? Like I had this brilliant idea, and if people just heard my pitch, I could turn it into a real career almost immediately. It just felt so clear to me in that moment. 

I know it probably sounds a little naive now, and I wasn't trying to be full of myself or anything. I just got really caught up in the excitement of it all. It's not a bad thing to believe in yourself, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound too out of touch with reality. Does that kind of answer your question?
During that time when you felt unusually confident or energized, did you notice that you needed less sleep than usual, like feeling rested after only a few hours of sleep?

Um, well... I guess I was staying up a bit later than normal. I really do try to take care of my health and get enough rest, I promise. But during that time... yeah, for several nights I think I only slept maybe three or four hours? 

But the thing is, I didn't feel exhausted at all. I actually woke up feeling really charged and ready to go. It honestly just felt like... like sleep was just getting in the way of finishing the next track or, um, updating my spreadsheets for the pitch. I just wanted to keep working while all those good ideas were flowing. 

I really hope that doesn't sound like I was being reckless with my health or doing something unhealthy on purpose. I just didn't feel like I needed the sleep right then because I was so into what I was doing. Is it normal to feel like that when you're just really inspired by a project? I hope I'm answering your question right.

Has there ever been a time when you felt so energized, confident, or irritable that it significantly affected your daily life or led to behaviors that were clearly out of character, even if only for a few days?

Um, well... I mean, I really don't want you to think I'm normally a difficult person to be around, because I always try to be polite and easygoing. But, um... yeah, right before I started feeling so down, I guess there was a stretch where I was feeling really, really fired up. 

Like, I was just so sure I was on a roll with everything I was doing. But because I was so focused, I think I might have been getting... well, maybe a little more easily annoyed than usual? It wasn't anything major, I promise. It's just that, um, if someone interrupted me while I was working on my music or my pitch, I might have snapped at them a little bit. 

I feel really bad about it now, because I'm not usually like that. I just felt so driven, you know? Like every little distraction was getting in the way of this huge breakthrough. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a jerk or anything. I was just really passionate in the moment. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about.

Have you ever had a period of time — even just a few days — when you were not just energetic or confident, but clearly and distinctly more so than your usual self to the point that other people could notice, or it led to behavior that was clearly out of character for you?

Um, well... I guess I was definitely a lot more active than usual during those days. I really try to stay organized and calm most of the time, I promise. But, um... I just had so much energy right then. 

It wasn't anything crazy, but I just couldn't really sit still. I kept bouncing back and forth between my computer, my MIDI controller, and all these notebooks where I was writing down ideas. It just felt like I had to keep moving to keep up with everything going on in my head. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I was totally out of control or acting weird. I was just really, really into the creative process, you know? Like I was just in the zone. I really hope that's an okay way to explain it... is that the kind of thing you were looking for?

Have you ever had a period lasting at least four consecutive days where you were clearly more energetic, confident, or irritable than usual — to the point where your behavior was noticeably different from your usual self, even if others didn’t say anything about it?

Um, well... I mean, I don't really think it was four whole days in a row? I try really hard to keep a steady routine, I really do. I don't want you to think I just go off the rails for days at a time. 

I know I said I had that burst of energy and was staying up late, but... I don't know if it was exactly four consecutive days of being noticeably different. Maybe it was just a couple of days where I was really focused, and then I just kind of needed to rest? I really hope I'm not confusing things. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it okay if I'm not entirely sure about the exact number of days?

Can you think back to that time when you felt more energetic and confident — was there a stretch of at least four days in a row where you felt clearly different from your usual self, even if only slightly, in terms of your mood, energy, or behavior?

Um, well... I've been thinking about it, and honestly, I really don't think it was four whole days in a row. I mean, I really don't want to give you the wrong idea, like I was just acting completely out of character for almost a week or something. I always try to keep things pretty balanced. 

It felt more like... maybe two or three days where I was just really, really productive and in a good mood? And then it just sort of fizzled out, and I went back to normal, or started feeling tired. I really hope that's helpful. I'm trying my best to remember, but I just don't think it lasted that long. Does that sound like it makes sense? I hope I'm not being difficult by not having a better answer for you.

Can you think back again to that time when you felt more energetic and confident — was there ever a stretch where you felt clearly different from your usual self for four or more days in a row, even if the change was mild?

Um, I... I'm sorry, I feel like I keep giving you the same answer, and I really don't want to frustrate you. I know you're trying to figure this out, and I want to be a good patient and help you do that. 

But, um... I really just can't remember a time when it lasted for four days straight. I promise I'm not trying to hide anything. It's just... I usually catch myself if I'm getting too wound up, you know? I try really hard not to let things get out of hand. So it's mostly just a day or two of feeling really good and getting things done, and then I make sure to settle back down. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that specific four-day thing you're asking about. Am I still giving you enough information to work with? I really hope I'm doing this right.
Can you tell me if you've had a period lasting at least two weeks where most of the time you felt down, lost interest in things, or experienced changes in your appetite, sleep, or energy levels?

Um, yeah... I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining all the time, because I know everyone gets sad sometimes. I try to stay positive, I really do. But... yeah, I guess I have had something like that. 

Looking back, I've had this sort of... depressed, slowed-down pattern kind of hanging around off and on for maybe about three months? I've been trying my best to push through it so I don't worry anyone. But I'd say the past few weeks have been the most noticeable, where it's been harder to shake off. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I just want to be honest with you so you can help. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
